{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZWqVHw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC-Abo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 37, "title": "Implement Ap real-mode IDTR load/store and interrupt-table relocation", "body": "## Problem

Ap has no IDTR state. `LIDT` and `SIDT` stop as unsupported, and every interrupt reads its vector from address zero. This leaves another prerequisite for DOS-extender initialization missing after #35/#36 added GDTR support.

Implement one coherent part of the protected-mode category: the real-mode interrupt-table register and its effect on existing interrupt delivery.

## Expected outcome

Ap supports `LIDT`, `SIDT`, relocated real-mode interrupt vectors and their table-limit failures. Default IDTR state preserves existing boot and interrupt behavior. VM retains its V30 decoder and fixed IVT.

Required hardware semantics:

- IDTR resets to base `0`, limit `03FFh`. `0F 01 /3` LIDT loads a little-endian limit and base; operand16 loads 24 base bits and clears the upper byte, while operand32 loads all 32. Address size is independent. Loading IDTR does not access the referenced table. Operand-boundary violations raise restartable exception 13, including SS-selected operands; register forms raise exception 6. See Intel486 PRM Table 10-1 and pp. 26-193–194. [Intel486 Programmer’s Reference Manual](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143).
- `0F 01 /1` SIDT stores exactly six bytes, including the full 32-bit base with either operand size, and preserves flags. LOCK raises exception 6. Use the explicit SIDT operation, while documenting the contradictory older compatibility text. The modern SS exception table also differs from the selected target-era exception contract above. [Intel SDM, SIDT operation and exceptions, printed pp. 4-643–644](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/782151/253667-sdm-vol-2b.pdf#page=645).
- Ap interrupt lookup uses `IDTR.base + 4 × vector`; the complete four-byte entry must fit the inclusive byte limit. Entries remain word offset/word segment pointers. Real-mode exceptions push no error code. An entry beyond the limit generates exception 8. [Intel486 PRM §22.3](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143).
- For an out-of-range software INT, the exception return address identifies the faulting instruction. If exception 8 itself has no available table entry, stop in bounded CPU shutdown rather than recurse indefinitely. Shutdown must remain distinct from ordinary HLT and recover through Machine reset. [Intel i486 datasheet §3.5 and Table 3.1, printed pp. 43–44](https://device.report/m/d0d81f608917b4fb1baa0da42c97dede73f88575259f19de2d24492a995d89ff).

Apply existing Bus mapping to operand and vector accesses, retaining unmasked linear metadata in IDTR. Preserve the established six-byte interrupt frame, saved-IP distinctions, IF/TF/AC handling, interrupt shadows and IRET behavior.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `27e5655302458cd09cac6eb7f6f54065a811b20f`.

Source inspection establishes:

- [Cpu::extended](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/27e5655302458cd09cac6eb7f6f54065a811b20f/src/cpu.rs#L614) accepts only `/0` and `/2` in group `0F 01`.
- [Cpu::deliver_interrupt](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/27e5655302458cd09cac6eb7f6f54065a811b20f/src/cpu.rs#L244) reads `vector * 4` without IDTR base or limit checks. IRQ, trap and exception callers currently turn delivery failures into host errors.
- [The existing unsupported-group test](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/27e5655302458cd09cac6eb7f6f54065a811b20f/tests/cpu386.rs#L961) explicitly expects `/1` and `/3` to fail. Replace those expectations with positive coverage; retain assertions for remaining unsupported operations and VM.

Minimal baseline reproduction for the Coordinator: place `0F 01 1E 00 40` (`LIDT [4000h]`) at an Ap instruction address with a valid stack and six-byte source. One CPU step currently returns `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 01 /3`. Expected behavior is an IDTR update and normal instruction completion.

Progress assessment: #35/#36 completed only the GDTR prerequisite. The Coordinator reports eight focused GDTR passes, 119 native integration passes and 50 production-Wasm browser passes, with an alternate-port browser configuration after port 8000 was occupied. These are attributed reports; this evaluation ran no builds or tests, and no separate review or CI-success report was supplied. [Recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/27e5655302458cd09cac6eb7f6f54065a811b20f/docs/validation.md#issue-35-ap-real-mode-gdtr-2026-10-23).

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied statuses and full scopes. Protected mode and CPU386 remain partial; paging and FPU remain unimplemented. No supplied open Issue duplicates this behavior.

Scope excludes CR0/PE transitions, protected gates, descriptors/caches, privilege transitions, LDTR/TR, task switching, paging, x87, NMI support, and a general nested-fault or invalid-stack overhaul. Those remain outstanding. Limit-induced shutdown is included only because programmable IDTR limits make it directly reachable. No Windows or new game research is required.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement per-CPU IDTR state, architectural reset values and both memory instructions. Add original `idtr_` Rust tests covering all four operand/address-size combinations, unaligned operands, ModR/M/SIB addressing, default SS and segment overrides. Assert exact six-byte stores with guards, high-base retention/clearing, preserved registers/flags, independent CPU instances and reset readback.
- [ ] Test `FFFAh` operand success and atomic faults at `FFFBh`, address32 `10000h` and `FFFFFFFFh`, for loads/stores and DS/SS. Verify exception vector, first-prefix saved IP, unchanged IDTR/destination and repair/IRET/retry. Register and LOCK forms must produce restartable exception 6. Keep handlers and stacks valid for these tests.
- [ ] Exercise relocated software INT, INT3, taken/untaken INTO, PIC-delivered IRQ, CPU fault, TF trap and public native interrupt injection. Install conflicting address-zero vectors so assertions prove relocation. Check exact frames, restart/resume addresses, IRET, AC clearing, IRQ acknowledgement/EOI and existing interrupt shadows.
- [ ] Test inclusive table limits: a complete final entry succeeds; reducing the limit by one routes an out-of-range INT to relocated vector 8 without a partial original frame. Verify its saved first-prefix IP and absence of an error-code word. A limit of `0023h` permits vector 8; `0022h` does not. The latter must reach bounded shutdown, resist subsequent stepping/maskable IRQ resumption, and recover after Machine reset without a host panic or recursive loop.
- [ ] Verify A20-off/on operand and relocated-vector mapping, ROM write protection for SIDT, and retained high IDTR base bits without dereferencing unmapped table memory during LIDT. Native and Wasm address arithmetic must agree.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built boot probe, offline preparation command, and manifest recording source/license, assembly commands, hashes, result bytes and a maximum two-million-slot budget. Suggested names are `guest/idtr.asm`, `tools/prepare_idtr_fixture.py` and `fixtures/idtr-manifest.json`. Run the identical probe natively and through production release Wasm at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after reset. Assert explicit PASS/FAIL, exact results/guards and unchanged disk bytes. Include bounded host assertions for a terminal shutdown case. Integrate preparation into existing CI; keep fixtures outside `web/`.
- [ ] Record a focused original test or unchanged probe failing on this baseline for the missing behavior and passing with the implementation. Preserve existing GDTR, CPULEVEL, hardware, DOS/application, VM and game regressions and their assertions; no proprietary software or ROM acquisition is required.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares the documented original/licensed fixtures and records successful `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 idtr_`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `python3 tools/build_media.py --check`, `python3 tools/build_font.py --check`, and `npm test` with both browser projects. Report exact commands, failures and environment substitutions; do not skip required assertions.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility and validation documentation with the implemented boundary, precise specification discrepancies and remaining feature parts. Passing these probes must not be presented as full protected-mode accuracy or commercial compatibility. Complete review and required checks before merge.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
